trigger: A Windows laptop operator or agent must validate First Mate harness readiness before crossing into WSL.
inputs: requested mode: contract, report, route, or runtime-floor
whether repository-owned WSL repair is authorized for this run
steps: Run the PowerShell-native front door Test-AgentSwitchboard-FirstMate-Harness.ps1 from the repository root or through its CMD wrapper.
For contract mode, run only Windows-safe Python contracts plus the PowerShell bridge ContractOnly gate; do not invoke bare bash from Windows Python.
Generate reports and route decisions through the Python owners without crossing into WSL.
Only runtime-floor mode may cross into WSL, and it must delegate to Test-AgentSwitchboard-FirstMate-WindowsWSL.ps1 with the exact HEAD.
If WSL repair is explicitly requested, use the existing repository-owned Repair-Technician-WSL-Ubuntu.cmd path and preserve its reboot boundary.
Preserve generated diagnostics and stop at the first real runtime dependency rather than substituting Android or another shell.
outputs: operator report or route artifact when requested
physical WSL floor artifacts only when runtime-floor executes
failure_handling: A bare bash invocation from Windows PowerShell or Windows Python is a harness routing defect, not proof that WSL or First Mate is broken.
A Windows path handed directly to a POSIX shell must be rejected or translated by the owning bridge; do not retry with ad-hoc quoting.
Preserve the failing command, exit code, and bounded diagnostics, repair the harness owner, and rerun the Windows-native front door.
proof_ceiling: contract/report/route modes prove harness behavior only; runtime-floor can prove the physical Windows-to-Ubuntu floor but not live crew productivity
